dedupe_keys.name: darkside ransomware attack on colonial pipeline may 2021 cyote case study

description: This Idaho National Laboratory case study analyses the DarkSide ransomware attack on Colonial Pipeline in May 2021 using the method of the Cybersecurity for the Operational Technology Environment (CyOTE) programme, funded by the Department of Energy office CESER. On 7 May 2021 a control centre employee found a ransom note on the enterprise network, and operators shut down 5,500 miles of pipeline that deliver refined fuel to about 260 points in 13 states to isolate the operational network; the outage caused shortages and higher petrol prices, the company paid 4.4 million dollars for a decryption tool, and operations restarted on 12 May. From public reports the study maps 11 MITRE ATT&CK for ICS techniques with 68 observables, from external remote services for initial access to loss of availability and loss of revenue, builds a timeline and attack graph, and lists observables and artefacts in appendices. Coverage: one incident, US East Coast fuel network. Access: 35-page PDF report INL/RPT-22-67337 of 31 March 2022, free. Licence and cost: US Government work, free. Caveats: based only on public information, with no access to Colonial's systems, and not updated since publication. It supports cascading failure and emergency response scenarios where a cyber incident stops fuel pipelines. It relates to the PHMSA incident data, the pipeline and grid cyber-physical incident panel, and the San Bruno pipeline case study in the catalogue.
